THIS PAGE WAS ABSENT FROM `annual-report-pages.csv` ENTIRELY: the table prints WHOLE DOLLARS with no cents, so the fifteen-money-figure recognition gate that admits a page to the tracker found one figure on it (`1.214,522`, a comma scanned as a stop) and the page was invisible -- the same defect that hid FY2018 p50 and FY2020 p46. FY2013: 19,825,315 + 4,473,351 = 24,298,666 exactly. A CAVEAT THE PAGE PRINTS ABOUT ITSELF, and it is rule 11's territory: footnote (1) reads `Principal amount only. THIS FILE is the `Outside the General Debt Limit` block: 3 purpose lines against the printed `Total Outside the General Debt Limit` in all five year columns.

rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30 2013`, PDF pages 81-82 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed pages 77-78). TWO LANDSCAPE PAGES, ONE TABLE, printed sideways with no text layer; both were rotated upright and read off their own 400 dpi bitmaps. The fiscal years run ACROSS: page 81 carries `2014` to `2030` and page 82 carries `2031` to `2047` and a final `TOTAL` column. Column names read off the printed header (rule 13b.4): the row labels used here are the page's own, verbatim -- `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL`, `GRAND TOTAL INTEREST`, `TOTAL DEBT` -- and each fiscal year is a ROW of this file because that is the grain the series runs in. THIS IS A PARTIAL READ AND THAT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING ON THIS CARD. ONLY THE THREE GRAND-TOTAL ROWS ARE TRANSCRIBED -- the town's whole debt service by year, FY2014 to FY2047, which is the series anybody would chart. THE PER-ISSUE ROWS ABOVE THEM ARE NOT READ: about ten borrowings, each printed as PRINCIPAL, INTEREST and a group total, across 34 year columns. So this file CANNOT say which bond ends in which year or what any single issue costs. That limit is already a registered row in `sources/data/money-gaps.csv` -- *What does each individual debt issue cost the town in a given year, and which of them fall off when?* -- and FY2013 belongs to it; no new gap is filed for it. THE CHECKS. (1) Each fiscal year states an identity: grand total principal plus grand total interest is total debt. 33 OF 34 YEARS CLOSE EXACTLY. (2) All three rows foot to the `TOTAL` column the table prints: principal 24,298,664 EXACTLY across 34 values, interest 7,307,840 within $1, total debt 31,187,800 within $1. THE TOLERANCE IS $1 AND HERE IS ITS DERIVATION. The schedule prints WHOLE DOLLARS over amounts that carry cents, so a printed total is the rounded sum and not the sum of the rounded parts. 34 addends; the observed maximum miss is $1 on two of the three rows. WHAT SAYS THIS IS ROUNDING AND NOT A MISREAD IS THE CONTRAST: `GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL` -- bond principal, which has no cents under it -- ties to its printed TOTAL EXACTLY at 24,298,664, while the two rows that do carry cents underneath each miss by exactly $1. The tolerance was not widened to make anything pass. AND FY2024 IS ATTESTED: THE TOWN'S OWN ARITHMETIC DISAGREES WITH ITSELF. The 2024 column prints GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL 846,635 and GRAND TOTAL INTEREST 120,310, which make 966,945, against a printed TOTAL DEBT of 548,241 -- the document out by 418,704. All three digits were re-read at 400 dpi in a tight crop of that column. TWO THINGS CORROBORATE IT and neither depends on the other. First, the SAME 418,704 is the amount by which the printed TOTAL column fails the same identity: 24,298,664 + 7,307,840 = 31,606,504 against a printed TOTAL DEBT total of 31,187,800. Second, each of the three rows separately foots to its own printed TOTAL (principal exactly, the other two within the declared $1), so the defect is one cell and not a column. WHICH CELL IS WRONG IS NOT ESTABLISHED. 846,635 less 418,704 is 427,931, and 418,704 is also the figure this report prints in the 2024 column of a `TOTAL MASS WATER POLL TRUST` row higher up the page -- that is an OBSERVATION about two figures being equal, not a cause, and nothing here tests whether the principal row double-counts a trust borrowing or the total-debt row omits one. THE FY2014 REPORT PRINTS THE SAME SCHEDULE A YEAR LATER and its `MASS WATER POOL 9*` row carries a principal of 418,704 in the FY2024 column with no interest and no total beside it -- the only such row in that 156-row schedule (fy2014-p40-debt-schedule.csv). Same amount, same year, same borrowing, different document. That LOCATES the discrepancy on the Mass Water Pool 9 balloon payment; it does not say which of FY2013's two figures is right. WHAT THIS IS (CLAUDE.md rule 11): scheduled debt SERVICE on borrowings outstanding at 30 June 2013. It is not an appropriation, it excludes anything borrowed since, and the figures are gross -- the MSBA and Mass Water Pollution Abatement Trust subsidies that pay part of some of these issues are not netted here and are not shown.

THE DOCUMENT, NOT THE READING. The 2024 column prints GRAND TOTAL PRINCIPAL 846,635 and GRAND TOTAL INTEREST 120,310 against a printed TOTAL DEBT of 548,241: out by 418,704. Re-read at 400 dpi. The printed TOTAL column fails the same identity by the same 418,704, and each of the three rows separately foots to its own printed TOTAL, so the defect is one cell. Which cell is wrong is not established. A THIRD, INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION, FROM ANOTHER DOCUMENT: the FY2014 annual town report prints the same schedule a year later, and `sources/data/page-reads/fy2014-p40-debt-schedule.csv` holds its `MASS WATER POOL 9*` row with a principal of 418,704 in the FY2024 column and NO interest and NO total printed beside it -- the only row in that whole 156-row schedule with a principal and no total. The same 418,704, in the same fiscal year, on the same borrowing, in a different report. That locates the FY2013 discrepancy on the Mass Water Pool 9 balloon payment. IT STILL DOES NOT SAY WHICH FIGURE IS RIGHT: the town may be excluding a subsidised trust payment from TOTAL DEBT deliberately, or the principal row may be double-counting it, and nothing in either report distinguishes those.

rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG / FY2013 COLLECTION OF TAXES`, PDF page 83 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed page 79). THE PAGE IS LANDSCAPE and has NO TEXT LAYER, so it was rotated upright and read off its own 400 dpi bitmap. COLUMN NAMES READ OFF THE PRINTED HEADER (rule 13b.4), verbatim and left to right: `COLLECTION OF TAXES`, `FORWARD`, `COMMITTMENTS` (the page's own spelling), `ADJUSTMENTS`, `REFUNDS`, `PAYMENTS`, `ABATEMENTS`, `TRANSFER`, `BALANCES`. Figures printed in parentheses are stored NEGATIVE, as the page prints them; `-` is the page's explicit zero. THE SCAN IS SKEWED AND THE LABEL COLUMN DRIFTS AGAINST THE FIGURES -- by the foot of the page a row label sits about one row pitch above its own figures, so NO ROW WAS ASSIGNED BY EYE. Each column's values were read in printed order and the assignment was settled by the arithmetic, which is rule 13b's own guarantee: a wrong layout cannot make real arithmetic close. TWO CHECKS, AND BOTH CLOSE COMPLETELY. (1) EVERY ROW STATES AN IDENTITY: forward + committments + adjustments + refunds + payments + abatements + transfer = balances. 57 OF 57 ROWS CLOSE TO THE CENT. (2) ALL EIGHT COLUMNS SUM TO THE `GRAND TOTAL` the page prints, to the cent: 1,651,248.72 / 22,523,058.03 / (25,688.60) / 93,375.26 / (22,091,835.42) / (171,928.23) / (317,778.88) / 1,660,450.88. No tolerance is declared and none was needed. ONE COLUMN ASSIGNMENT WAS CORRECTED BY THE TOTALS AND IS WORTH RECORDING. Five figures in the betterment and sewer block -- (434.57), (104.59), (5,390.09), (2,862.44) and (28,226.44) -- were first placed in ABATEMENTS. The row identities still closed, because both columns add, but the COLUMN totals came out exactly 37,018.13 wrong in opposite directions. Those five sum to 37,018.13, they sit at the same x as the (281.32) on the TAX LIENS row, and the ABATEMENTS column is empty throughout that block. A row identity alone could not have caught it; the printed column totals did. WHAT THIS IS. A receivable is money BILLED and not yet collected, by levy year and by kind -- motor vehicle excise (MVE), personal property (PP), real estate (RE), supplementals, tax liens, rollback taxes and the betterment and sewer commitments. It is NOT revenue and it is NOT an appropriation. The FY2013 receipts page (PDF page 63) counts what came IN; this page counts what is still owed.

rows.proof: `FY 2014 Omnibus Budget`, PDF pages 87-88 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed pages 83-84): the budget as VOTED at the Annual Town Meeting, printed in the warrant section at the back of the report. NEITHER PAGE HAS A TEXT LAYER; both were read off their own 400 dpi bitmaps. COLUMN NAMES READ OFF THE PRINTED HEADER (rule 13b.4), verbatim: `Line No.`, `Account`, `VOTED FY 2014`. Each page prints TWO column-pairs, read left to right; `-` is the page's explicit zero and is read as 0.00, never as an absent figure. THE CHECK, AND IT CLOSES TWICE OVER. 90 line items against eleven printed section totals -- every section foots to its own printed total EXACTLY (Maturing Debt 2,863,179; Gen Gov Unclassified 2,624,099; General Government 1,157,634; Central Purchasing 54,015; Protection 2,485,434; Health & Sanitation 64,090; DPW 1,616,559; Assistance 122,507; Schools 16,831,683; Library 355,563; Recreation 2,500) -- and the eleven section totals sum to the printed `TOTAL OMNIBUS BUDGET` of 28,177,263.00, also exactly. No tolerance is declared and none was needed. THE FIVE SUB-SUBTOTALS ARE `line` AND NOT SUMMED: Subtotal Police 1,356,895, Subtotal Fire Dept. 947,845 and Subtotal Other Protection 180,694 are inside Total Protection, and Subtotal C.O.A. 99,647 and Subtotal Veterans 22,860 are inside Total Assistance. Each of those five also foots to its own members exactly; they are kept out of the sum so nothing is counted twice. THE PRINTED LINE NUMBERS SKIP 18 -- the page runs 17, 19 -- and that is recorded as printed, not repaired. WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT (CLAUDE.md rules 1 and 11). This is the FY2014 budget AS VOTED, printed in the FY2013 report. It is a BUDGET, not an actual, and it may not be differenced against any expended column. Every line is a NET general-fund appropriation: grants, revolving funds, fees and the circuit breaker pay for real staff and appear nowhere here, so a line that rises may mean a grant ended rather than that the town bought more. SIBLING: `sources/data/table-corrections.csv` already carries three `read` rows for page 88 of this report -- line 65 Town Highway Garage 1,000.00, line 75 Veterans' Benefits 17,500.00 and line 76 Veteran's Administration 4,250.00, recorded 28 September 2026 against the generic `appropriations` extract. THIS INDEPENDENT READ CONFIRMS ALL THREE to the cent.

rows.proof: `CALENDAR 2013 WAGES`, PDF pages 93-97 of the FY2013 annual town report (printed pages 89-93): every person the Town paid in calendar 2013, with their department and their gross wages. Five pages, 544 names. NO PAGE HAS A TEXT LAYER; each was read off its own 400 dpi bitmap. PAGE 93 IS THE FIRST PAGE OF THIS RUN AND IT WAS NOT IN THE PAGE TRACKER. The tracker admits a page on fifteen recognised money figures and recognition found seventeen words on this one, so it was ABSENT rather than unfinished -- 130 names, A to D, invisible to every count of what remains. It was found by sweeping every page of the report for money figures against the tracker's own list, which is the extent check `READING-A-REPORT-PAGE.md` prescribes. THE COLUMN NAMES HERE ARE OURS, AND THAT IS SAID RATHER THAN HIDDEN. The only thing printed over this table is `CALENDAR 2013 WAGES`, above the money column. The three columns to its left carry NO printed heading at all, so `fund_number` (surname), `fund_name` (forename and department) and `gross_wages` are labels WE have given to what the cells visibly contain. Rule 13b.4 says never infer a column name from the words at the top of a page; here there are no words to infer from, and the honest statement is that the document does not name them. EACH PAGE PRINTS TWO LABEL/NAME/DEPARTMENT/AMOUNT COLUMN-PAIRS and they are ONE list, not two: page 93 runs ADAMOWICZ to BRAND down the left and BRANHAM to DAVIS down the right, so the alphabet continues from one pair into the next. That is unlike FY2022, whose two columns are separately alphabetised A-Z and must not be merged; it was checked here rather than assumed. THE PAGES PRINT NO TOTAL OF ANY KIND -- not per page, not per department, not for the run -- so there is no arithmetic to close and THE CHECK IS COVERAGE, declared and weaker. Two assertions, and they catch different failures: `rows_per_page` = 130, which every page but the last carries exactly (the last carries 24), catches a single name skipped; and `ordered_by` surname, which runs forward through all 544 rows without going backwards once, catches a page or a block dropped. NEITHER CAN SEE A MISREAD DIGIT. A wrong figure in this file survives both checks untouched, and nothing in the archive states these wages a second time. READ AS PRINTED, INCLUDING WHERE THE PAGE TRUNCATES. Several surnames are cut off by their cell and are recorded truncated rather than guessed: `CARPENTER BO`, `COURTEMANC`, `MCCARTHY-GU`, `MITCHELL-TAR`, `PAPADOPOULO`, `VAILLANCOUR`. `MC CARTHY` is printed with a space and `MCBRIDE` without, on adjacent rows, and both stand. WHAT THIS IS AND IS NOT (CLAUDE.md rules 7 and 11). It is GROSS WAGES PAID in a CALENDAR year to named people, by the department that paid them. It is NOT a fiscal-year figure, so it cannot be differenced against any budget line in this report, which are all FY2013. It is NOT a headcount of positions: a person paid by two departments appears twice, and a name with $48.00 beside it and a name with $126,540.42 are one row each. It carries NO FTE and NO funding source, so it cannot say whether a post was full time or which fund paid for it -- the same limit the staff rosters have, already registered in `money-gaps.csv`. And it is wages only: it excludes every benefit, so it is not what any of these people cost the town.
